candidates.section: Expected Behavior
candidates.text:
### Expected Behavior

A heartbeat ack is a one-shot reply to a client request, like a toast is a one-shot notification. It should survive the interrupted-run queue clear, or be sent directly rather than queued, so that one heartbeat always produces one ack.

candidates.section: Steps To Reproduce
candidates.text:
### Steps To Reproduce

1) Run the app
2) Upload any file
3) Click on the "Disable" button

At this point, notice how you can't click the `file_uplaoder` to change the file.
Also note what the number of reruns is.
Finally, notice how the script can indeed see a file was uploaded (as shown in `st.info`)

Also note that the number of reruns has increased (this is not good).
Finally, notice how the script can detect `file_uploader` no longer storing a file.

candidates.title: button-behavior-and-examples
candidates.section: Logic nested in a button with a rerun
candidates.text:
#### Logic nested in a button with a rerun

Although callbacks are often preferred to avoid extra reruns, our first 'John Doe'/'Jane Doe' example can be modified by adding [`st.rerun`](/develop/api-reference/execution-flow/st.rerun) instead. If you need to acces data in `st.session_state` before the button that modifies it, you can include `st.rerun` to rerun the script after the change has been committed. This means the script will rerun twice when a button is clicked.

```python
import streamlit as st
import pandas as pd

if 'name' not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state['name'] = 'John Doe'

st.header(st.session_state['name'])

if st.button('Jane'):
    st.session_state['name'] = 'Jane Doe'
    st.rerun()

if st.button('John'):
    st.session_state['name'] = 'John Doe'
    st.rerun()

st.header(st.session_state['name'])
```

candidates.title: Add page and app descriptions (`page_description`, `st.Page`, `st.App`)
candidates.section: How?
candidates.text:
```python
app = st.App(
    "main.py",
    title="Finance apps",
    description=(
        "Internal finance dashboards. Net revenue excludes refunds and is in EUR."
    ),
)
```

Suggested behavior:

- `st.Page.description` is the default for that page; `st.set_page_config(page_description=...)` overrides it for the current run (same additive pattern as today's page title).
- Single-page apps that never call `st.Page` still get a description via `set_page_config`.
- `st.App` title/description are app-level and static. They do not replace per-page title/description. For `streamlit run` apps without `st.App`, the default page's title/description (or a future config option) can stand in.
- Consumers of the same strings: HTML `<meta name="description">` / Open Graph, assistive tech, navigation (if we choose to surface it), and structured snapshots / a static app descriptor.

**Naming.** `page_description` on `set_page_config` matches `page_title`. On `st.Page` and `st.App`, `description` / `title` match the existing `title` parameter (the [agent-app interface spec](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/docs/agent-app-interface/specs/2026-08-28-agent-app-interface/product-spec.md) also floated `app_title` / `app_description` on `st.App` if we want the prefix explicit).

**Not in this request:** element-level alternative text for images, charts, and tables (#8563) and `help` on media (#3133). Arbitrary extra `<meta>` tags (GSC verification, etc.) stay with #16634.

parent.title: Add page and app descriptions (`page_description`, `st.Page`, `st.App`)
parent.text:
### How?

**Page description on `st.set_page_config`**, matching `page_title` / `page_icon`:

```python
st.set_page_config(
    page_title="Regional revenue",
    page_icon=":material/payments:",
    page_description=(
        "Net revenue by billing region. Excludes refunds. Periods are UTC."
    ),
)
```

**Optional `description` on `st.Page`**, so the page list carries copy without running each page (consistent with `title` / `icon`, not `page_*`):

```python
st.Page(
    "revenue.py",
    title="Regional revenue",
    icon=":material/payments:",
    description="Net revenue by billing region. Excludes refunds.",
)
```

**Static title and description on `st.App`**, available without executing the script:

```python
app = st.App(
    "main.py",
    title="Finance apps",
    description=(
        "Internal finance dashboards. Net revenue excludes refunds and is in EUR."
    ),
)
```

Suggested behavior:

- `st.Page.description` is the default for that page; `st.set_page_config(page_description=...)` overrides it for the current run (same additive pattern as today's page title).
- Single-page apps that never call `st.Page` still get a description via `set_page_config`.
- `st.App` title/description are app-level and static. They do not replace per-page title/description. For `streamlit run` apps without `st.App`, the default page's title/description (or a future config option) can stand in.
- Consumers of the same strings: HTML `<meta name="description">` / Open Graph, assistive tech, navigation (if we choose to surface it), and structured snapshots / a static app descriptor.

**Naming.** `page_description` on `set_page_config` matches `page_title`. On `st.Page` and `st.App`, `description` / `title` match the existing `title` parameter (the [agent-app interface spec](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/docs/agent-app-interface/specs/2026-08-28-agent-app-interface/product-spec.md) also floated `app_title` / `app_description` on `st.App` if we want the prefix explicit).

**Not in this request:** element-level alternative text for images, charts, and tables (#8563) and `help` on media (#3133). Arbitrary extra `<meta>` tags (GSC verification, etc.) stay with #16634.

Although callbacks are often preferred to avoid extra reruns, our first 'John Doe'/'Jane Doe' example can be modified by adding [`st.rerun`](/develop/api-reference/execution-flow/st.rerun) instead. If you need to acces data in `st.session_state` before the button that modifies it, you can include `st.rerun` to rerun the script after the change has been committed. This means the script will rerun twice when a button is clicked.

```python
import streamlit as st
import pandas as pd

if 'name' not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state['name'] = 'John Doe'

st.header(st.session_state['name'])

if st.button('Jane'):
    st.session_state['name'] = 'Jane Doe'
    st.rerun()

if st.button('John'):
    st.session_state['name'] = 'John Doe'
    st.rerun()

st.header(st.session_state['name'])
```

context.title: Add page and app descriptions (`page_description`, `st.Page`, `st.App`)
context.text:
- `st.Page.description` is the default for that page; `st.set_page_config(page_description=...)` overrides it for the current run (same additive pattern as today's page title).
- Single-page apps that never call `st.Page` still get a description via `set_page_config`.
- `st.App` title/description are app-level and static. They do not replace per-page title/description. For `streamlit run` apps without `st.App`, the default page's title/description (or a future config option) can stand in.
- Consumers of the same strings: HTML `<meta name="description">` / Open Graph, assistive tech, navigation (if we choose to surface it), and structured snapshots / a static app descriptor.

**Naming.** `page_description` on `set_page_config` matches `page_title`. On `st.Page` and `st.App`, `description` / `title` match the existing `title` parameter (the [agent-app interface spec](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/docs/agent-app-interface/specs/2026-08-28-agent-app-interface/product-spec.md) also floated `app_title` / `app_description` on `st.App` if we want the prefix explicit).
context.section: Add page and app descriptions (`page_description`, `st.Page`, `st.App`) > How?

parent.title: Add page and app descriptions (`page_description`, `st.Page`, `st.App`)
parent.text:
### How?

**Page description on `st.set_page_config`**, matching `page_title` / `page_icon`:

```python
st.set_page_config(
    page_title="Regional revenue",
    page_icon=":material/payments:",
    page_description=(
        "Net revenue by billing region. Excludes refunds. Periods are UTC."
    ),
)
```

**Optional `description` on `st.Page`**, so the page list carries copy without running each page (consistent with `title` / `icon`, not `page_*`):

```python
st.Page(
    "revenue.py",
    title="Regional revenue",
    icon=":material/payments:",
    description="Net revenue by billing region. Excludes refunds.",
)
```

**Static title and description on `st.App`**, available without executing the script:

```python
app = st.App(
    "main.py",
    title="Finance apps",
    description=(
        "Internal finance dashboards. Net revenue excludes refunds and is in EUR."
    ),
)
```

Suggested behavior:

- `st.Page.description` is the default for that page; `st.set_page_config(page_description=...)` overrides it for the current run (same additive pattern as today's page title).
- Single-page apps that never call `st.Page` still get a description via `set_page_config`.
- `st.App` title/description are app-level and static. They do not replace per-page title/description. For `streamlit run` apps without `st.App`, the default page's title/description (or a future config option) can stand in.
- Consumers of the same strings: HTML `<meta name="description">` / Open Graph, assistive tech, navigation (if we choose to surface it), and structured snapshots / a static app descriptor.

**Naming.** `page_description` on `set_page_config` matches `page_title`. On `st.Page` and `st.App`, `description` / `title` match the existing `title` parameter (the [agent-app interface spec](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/docs/agent-app-interface/specs/2026-08-28-agent-app-interface/product-spec.md) also floated `app_title` / `app_description` on `st.App` if we want the prefix explicit).

**Not in this request:** element-level alternative text for images, charts, and tables (#8563) and `help` on media (#3133). Arbitrary extra `<meta>` tags (GSC verification, etc.) stay with #16634.

context.title: file_uploader allows to remove files despite disabled = True
context.text:
### Steps To Reproduce

1) Run the app
2) Upload any file
3) Click on the "Disable" button

At this point, notice how you can't click the `file_uplaoder` to change the file.
Also note what the number of reruns is.
Finally, notice how the script can indeed see a file was uploaded (as shown in `st.info`)

4) Click on the X at the right of the uploaded filename

At this point, notice how you still can't click the `file_uplaoder` to change the file (which if good).
Also note that the number of reruns has increased (this is not good).
Finally, notice how the script can detect `file_uploader` no longer storing a file.

candidates.text:
#### Logic nested in a button with a rerun

Although callbacks are often preferred to avoid extra reruns, our first 'John Doe'/'Jane Doe' example can be modified by adding [`st.rerun`](/develop/api-reference/execution-flow/st.rerun) instead. If you need to acces data in `st.session_state` before the button that modifies it, you can include `st.rerun` to rerun the script after the change has been committed. This means the script will rerun twice when a button is clicked.

```python
import streamlit as st
import pandas as pd

if 'name' not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state['name'] = 'John Doe'

st.header(st.session_state['name'])

if st.button('Jane'):
    st.session_state['name'] = 'Jane Doe'
    st.rerun()

if st.button('John'):
    st.session_state['name'] = 'John Doe'
    st.rerun()

st.header(st.session_state['name'])
```

context.title: Add page and app descriptions (`page_description`, `st.Page`, `st.App`)
context.text:
- `st.Page.description` is the default for that page; `st.set_page_config(page_description=...)` overrides it for the current run (same additive pattern as today's page title).
- Single-page apps that never call `st.Page` still get a description via `set_page_config`.
- `st.App` title/description are app-level and static. They do not replace per-page title/description. For `streamlit run` apps without `st.App`, the default page's title/description (or a future config option) can stand in.
- Consumers of the same strings: HTML `<meta name="description">` / Open Graph, assistive tech, navigation (if we choose to surface it), and structured snapshots / a static app descriptor.

**Naming.** `page_description` on `set_page_config` matches `page_title`. On `st.Page` and `st.App`, `description` / `title` match the existing `title` parameter (the [agent-app interface spec](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/docs/agent-app-interface/specs/2026-08-28-agent-app-interface/product-spec.md) also floated `app_title` / `app_description` on `st.App` if we want the prefix explicit).
context.section: Add page and app descriptions (`page_description`, `st.Page`, `st.App`) > How?

parent.title: Add page and app descriptions (`page_description`, `st.Page`, `st.App`)
parent.text:
### How?

**Page description on `st.set_page_config`**, matching `page_title` / `page_icon`:

```python
st.set_page_config(
    page_title="Regional revenue",
    page_icon=":material/payments:",
    page_description=(
        "Net revenue by billing region. Excludes refunds. Periods are UTC."
    ),
)
```

**Optional `description` on `st.Page`**, so the page list carries copy without running each page (consistent with `title` / `icon`, not `page_*`):

```python
st.Page(
    "revenue.py",
    title="Regional revenue",
    icon=":material/payments:",
    description="Net revenue by billing region. Excludes refunds.",
)
```

**Static title and description on `st.App`**, available without executing the script:

```python
app = st.App(
    "main.py",
    title="Finance apps",
    description=(
        "Internal finance dashboards. Net revenue excludes refunds and is in EUR."
    ),
)
```

Suggested behavior:

- `st.Page.description` is the default for that page; `st.set_page_config(page_description=...)` overrides it for the current run (same additive pattern as today's page title).
- Single-page apps that never call `st.Page` still get a description via `set_page_config`.
- `st.App` title/description are app-level and static. They do not replace per-page title/description. For `streamlit run` apps without `st.App`, the default page's title/description (or a future config option) can stand in.
- Consumers of the same strings: HTML `<meta name="description">` / Open Graph, assistive tech, navigation (if we choose to surface it), and structured snapshots / a static app descriptor.

**Naming.** `page_description` on `set_page_config` matches `page_title`. On `st.Page` and `st.App`, `description` / `title` match the existing `title` parameter (the [agent-app interface spec](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/docs/agent-app-interface/specs/2026-08-28-agent-app-interface/product-spec.md) also floated `app_title` / `app_description` on `st.App` if we want the prefix explicit).

**Not in this request:** element-level alternative text for images, charts, and tables (#8563) and `help` on media (#3133). Arbitrary extra `<meta>` tags (GSC verification, etc.) stay with #16634.

context.title: file_uploader allows to remove files despite disabled = True
context.text:
### Steps To Reproduce

1) Run the app
2) Upload any file
3) Click on the "Disable" button

At this point, notice how you can't click the `file_uplaoder` to change the file.
Also note what the number of reruns is.
Finally, notice how the script can indeed see a file was uploaded (as shown in `st.info`)

4) Click on the X at the right of the uploaded filename

At this point, notice how you still can't click the `file_uplaoder` to change the file (which if good).
Also note that the number of reruns has increased (this is not good).
Finally, notice how the script can detect `file_uploader` no longer storing a file.

context.text:
### Expected Behavior

A heartbeat ack is a one-shot reply to a client request, like a toast is a one-shot notification. It should survive the interrupted-run queue clear, or be sent directly rather than queued, so that one heartbeat always produces one ack.
